original_question: For the potentially good reduction case in Proposition 6.19, what is the ramification filtration of the wild monodromy group?
target_in_paper: Question 6.20 in Section 6.2.2 (immediately after Proposition 6.19) of the subsection "Automorphisms of curves and stable reduction".
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the exact local place in the paper: it singles out the potentially good reduction case of Proposition 6.19 and asks for the ramification filtration of the wild monodromy group, which is precisely the content of Question 6.20.
missing_details: The ambient local field should be stated: K = Q_p^tame, with valuation ring R, as in Proposition 6.19.
The curve under discussion should be named explicitly: a p-cyclic cover C -> P^1_K birationally given by Z^p = f(X) = 1 + cX^q + X^{q+1}.
The parameter q should be defined explicitly as q = p^s.
The coefficient condition on c from Proposition 6.19(b) is left implicit in the draft; this is the specific potentially good reduction case singled out by that proposition.

The meaning of "wild monodromy group" should be defined: it is the p-Sylow subgroup Gal(L/K)_w of the finite monodromy group Gal(L/K), where L/K is the minimal finite Galois extension over which C acquires semistable reduction.
The known structure of the group in the Proposition 6.19(b) case should be included: extraspecial of order p q^2 and exponent p for p > 2, and the indicated central product of Q8 and D8's for p = 2.

To be fully stand-alone, the question should make clear that the filtration asked for is the ramification filtration attached to the local Galois extension L/K, not merely an abstract subgroup filtration.

The draft does not mention the surrounding scope: this question appears in the inverse-Galois/monodromy discussion of Section 6.2.2, after the authors ask whether maximal wild monodromy can occur for a prescribed degeneration type.
refined_question: Let K = Q_p^tame with valuation ring R, let q = p^s, and let C/K be the p-cyclic cover of P^1_K birationally given by Z^p = 1 + cX^q + X^{q+1}. In the specific case of Proposition 6.19(b), where C has potentially good reduction and the wild monodromy group Gal(L/K)_w of the finite monodromy extension L/K is known to be extraspecial of order p q^2 and exponent p when p > 2 (and, for p = 2, the corresponding central product built from Q8 and D8), determine the ramification filtration of Gal(L/K)_w.
justification: The paper’s official formulation closest to your draft is not a new conjecture or theorem elsewhere, but exactly Question 6.20, which follows Proposition 6.19 in Section 6.2.2. Definition 6.14 supplies the meaning of finite monodromy and wild monodromy, while the surrounding discussion in Sections 6.2, 6.2.1, and 6.2.2 explains that the authors are studying explicit p-cyclic covers over p-adic fields, asking for maximality and then finer ramification-theoretic structure of the resulting monodromy extensions. Because your draft explicitly points to Proposition 6.19 and the potentially good reduction case, Question 6.20 is the exact target and should not be broadened to the neighboring Questions 6.21 or 6.22.
